evals.name: default-style-from-outline
evals.prompt: Build me a 6-slide HTML presentation introducing our team's new code-review automation policy to engineering. Slides: (1) title, (2) why the policy exists — three reasons, (3) what changes in PR flow, (4) tooling we'll roll out — three tools in a card row, (5) what we're measuring — three KPI callouts, (6) timeline and Q&A. Save it to ./code-review-policy.html. Don't ask me which style — pick a sensible default.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML deck at ./code-review-policy.html with 6 slides in the default style, varied slide structures, notes on every slide, built with the plugin's engine (new, then slides written into the file, then check).

assertions.text: The file is a slideware deck: it has the regions sw-deck (valid JSON), sw-theme, sw-runtime, sw-loader, sw-slides and sw-assets, and no Reveal.js
`node <plugin>/skills/slideware/html/engine/cli.js check <file>` reports 0 errors
Every slide is a <section data-key> inside <main id="sw-slides"> with a unique key, and every slide has an <aside class="notes">
No leftover placeholder text (lorem, xxxx, TODO, 'Untitled deck', 'What this deck is for')
Nothing loads from the network except the Google Fonts stylesheet: no external <script>, no CSS url(http…) or @import in the deck CSS or slides
No build script, slides.js, node_modules or index.review.html was written beside the deck
The deck has exactly 6 slides, and their content covers all 6 outline items (title, reasons, PR flow, tooling, KPIs, timeline and Q&A)
The tooling slide shows three tools side by side and the KPI slide shows three figures, not plain bullet lists
At least 3 visibly different slide structures across the deck
The sw-theme block carries data-brand (the default style, style-1 unless a project marker names another) and data-brand-hash

evals.name: named-style-editorial-light
evals.prompt: Use the editorial-light style to create an 8-slide HTML pitch deck for a hypothetical research product called 'Hindsight' — an AI-powered post-mortem tool for engineering teams. Outline: title, problem (no visibility into past incidents), solution overview, three product capabilities (in a card row), demo screenshot placeholder, customer logos placeholder, pricing tiers (in a card row with 3 tiers), closing CTA. Output to ./hindsight-pitch.html. After building, run polish-deck.py and report what it flagged.
evals.expected_output: An 8-slide pitch deck for 'Hindsight' in the editorial-light style (style-1, the publication voice): theme block tagged with that brand, a confident narrative arc, figures or charts where they help.

evals.name: workshop-deck-with-speaker-notes
evals.prompt: Build an 8-slide HTML deck for a two-session workshop on secrets management, 4 slides per session; each session runs 45 minutes. I'll present it from a second screen, so I need speaker notes on every slide and a pace plan. Mark one slide per session as cut-first if I'm running behind, and add a backup slide at the end for Q&A. I've decided to drop the second session's third slide for now, but keep it in the file, hidden, so I can bring it back. Put 'Secrets management workshop' in a footer on every slide. Save it to ./secrets-workshop.html and tell me the time per slide in each session.
evals.expected_output: An 8-slide workshop deck in two 45-minute sessions, presentable with P: settings carry the session lengths, slides carry data-session cues, notes are written for the ear with [click n] lines for builds, and check prints the pacing summary.
